stories.headline: Pitch invader steals Rahmanullah Gurbaz's cap mid-match and runs away
stories.what: In a bizarre incident during a live cricket match, a fan invaded the pitch and stole Afghanistan wicketkeeper-batter Rahmanullah Gurbaz's cap before running away, with the moment captured on video. The incident, reported by The Times of India, highlights ongoing concerns about ground security and spectator management at cricket venues. Gurbaz's reaction and the response of security personnel were also caught on camera.
stories.lens: Pitch invasions and security breaches at live sporting events are a growing concern for cricket administrators and venue managers globally, including in India.
stories.article:
A fan stormed the pitch during a live cricket match and brazenly stole Rahmanullah Gurbaz's cap before making a run for it, with the entire episode captured on video and quickly going viral. The incident, reported by The Times of India, has reignited debate about the adequacy of security measures at cricket stadiums.

Gurbaz, Afghanistan's explosive wicketkeeper-batter and one of the most recognisable faces in Twenty20 cricket, found himself at the centre of the unusual moment mid-match. The pitch invader's swift entry, theft, and attempted escape in full view of players, officials, and spectators made for a dramatic and deeply embarrassing episode for the ground authorities.

Security personnel were left scrambling to intercept the fan, but not before the theft was completed in plain sight. Such incidents not only disrupt play and unsettle players but also raise serious questions about the protocols in place to protect players' safety and dignity on the field.

Cricket's governing bodies have increasingly been called upon to enforce stricter perimeter security and harsher penalties for pitch invasions. This latest episode is likely to prompt a fresh review of safety standards, particularly as high-profile international fixtures attract larger and more excitable crowds.
key_facts: Fan invaded the pitch and stole Rahmanullah Gurbaz's cap
Incident occurred mid-match and was caught on video
Raises fresh concerns about cricket venue security

stories.headline: India and Japan to celebrate 75 years of ties with cricket, art and anime events in 2027
stories.what: India and Japan will mark the 75th anniversary of their diplomatic relationship in 2027 with a series of cultural and sporting events, including cricket, art exhibitions, and anime-themed activities. The celebrations are intended to deepen people-to-people ties between the two nations and showcase the breadth of their bilateral relationship. The inclusion of cricket as a centrepiece reflects the sport's growing reach and India's cultural soft power globally.
stories.lens: Cricket being chosen as a symbol of India-Japan friendship in 2027 reflects the sport's expanding global footprint and India's growing cultural influence in Asia.
stories.article:
India and Japan are set to celebrate the 75th anniversary of their diplomatic ties in 2027 through a rich programme of events spanning cricket, art, and anime, reflecting the multifaceted nature of the two nations' relationship. The announcement, reported by The Hindu, signals a deliberate effort by both governments to use culture and sport as bridges between their peoples.

The inclusion of cricket is particularly noteworthy: it underscores how Indian soft power — anchored by the sport's massive popularity — is being projected into East Asia. Japan has been steadily developing its own cricket ecosystem, and joint events in 2027 could further accelerate the game's grassroots growth there.

Anime, Japan's globally beloved animation tradition, sits alongside art exhibitions as part of the cultural package, highlighting a reciprocal exchange — India celebrating what Japan has given the world culturally, while Japan engages with cricket as an Indian cultural export. Such exchanges have traditionally strengthened bilateral goodwill at the public level beyond formal diplomatic channels.

The 2027 programme is still in planning stages, but its ambition and variety suggest that both governments are committed to a genuinely substantial anniversary. For India's cricket administrators and cultural diplomats alike, the events represent an opportunity to expand the game's footprint across Asia.
key_facts: India-Japan 75th diplomatic anniversary to be marked in 2027
Events will include cricket, art, and anime-themed activities
Celebration aims to strengthen people-to-people ties

stories.headline: James Coles and Josh Tongue named in England's 16-member squad for India ODIs
stories.what: England have announced a 16-member squad for the upcoming ODI series against India, with James Coles and Josh Tongue named in the side. The squad announcement signals England's planning for the longer-format white-ball series that follows the T20Is. Coles and Tongue's inclusions are seen as significant selections, bringing a mix of youth and pace to England's ODI setup.
stories.lens: The squad named for the India ODIs will shape the next major chapter of one of cricket's biggest rivalries, and these selections give fans a clear look at England's plans.
stories.article:
England have named their 16-member squad for the ODI series against India, with James Coles and Josh Tongue both earning places in the side. The announcement, confirmed by NDTV Sports, outlines England's white-ball ambitions as they prepare to face India in a format that carries significant ICC ranking implications.

Coles's inclusion is notable for the young player, representing recognition of his potential at the international level. Tongue, a right-arm pace bowler, adds variety and raw pace to an England attack that will need to be at its best to challenge a well-rounded Indian ODI batting order.

The 16-member squad gives England's management flexibility in terms of team composition and allows them to trial options ahead of future ICC events. Selection debates are certain to follow, particularly around who makes the final playing XI once the series begins.

For Indian fans, the ODI squad announcement is an early indicator of the competition awaiting their team. With the T20I series still live, attention will soon shift to what promises to be a fiercely competitive ODI encounter.
key_facts: James Coles named in England's 16-member ODI squad vs India
Josh Tongue also included in the squad
Squad is for the upcoming ODI series against India

stories.headline: Gavaskar blasts Indian team for 2-0 series loss to Ireland
stories.what: Cricket legend Sunil Gavaskar has sharply criticised the Indian team after they suffered a 2-0 series defeat to Ireland, calling it one of the 'worst days' for Indian cricket. The whitewash by Ireland marks a stunning upset, with Gavaskar making clear his disappointment at the performance. His remarks reflect the depth of shock within the cricketing establishment at India's failure against a team historically considered among the lower-ranked sides.
stories.lens: A 2-0 series loss to Ireland — once considered minnows — is a wake-up call for Indian cricket's selection and form ahead of busier international commitments.
stories.article:
Sunil Gavaskar has delivered a stinging rebuke to the Indian cricket team following their 2-0 series defeat to Ireland, labelling it among the 'worst days' in recent memory for Indian cricket. The legendary opener's public outburst signals just how badly the result has shaken the country's cricketing establishment.

For Ireland, it is a landmark achievement — a clean sweep of a full series against India, a side that consistently ranks among the world's best. Ireland coach and team officials have been quick to point out that the victory is a reflection of their growing stature in the international game, with team representative O'Donnell noting that the series win boosts Ireland's status in international cricket.

Gavaskar's remarks will intensify pressure on the Indian selectors and team management to scrutinise the playing XI, team composition, and approach in limited-overs cricket outside the traditional bilateral series against top-ranked nations. The loss raises pointed questions about India's bench strength and preparation for players given opportunities on such tours.

The defeat is likely to trigger a broader conversation about how India manages its squad rotation on away tours against emerging nations. With the England T20I series already underway, the team will need to regroup quickly, though the sting of Ireland's historic win will linger for some time.
key_facts: India lost 2-0 to Ireland in the series
Gavaskar called it the 'worst days' for Indian cricket
Ireland's O'Donnell says win boosts Ireland's international stature

stories.headline: Jofra Archer returns as England make two changes for 2nd T20I against India
stories.what: England have named their playing XI for the second T20I against India, with fast bowler Jofra Archer making a notable return to the side. The hosts have made two changes from the first match of the series. Archer's inclusion adds significant pace and experience to England's attack and signals a stronger intent to level or take the series against India.
stories.lens: Archer's return to the England T20I side against India is a major tactical shift that could directly influence the outcome of this series for millions of Indian cricket fans watching.
stories.article:
England have made two significant changes to their playing XI for the second T20I against India, with the most eye-catching being the return of fast bowler Jofra Archer. The selection marks a meaningful upgrade in England's bowling attack for the high-profile fixture.

Archer, who has battled injury setbacks over recent years, brings genuine pace and the ability to trouble even the most accomplished batting line-ups. His inclusion against a strong Indian side underlines England's determination to push back after the first T20I and signals they are not taking the series lightly.

The two changes England have made suggest their team management has been proactive in addressing any weaknesses exposed in the opening match. The precise nature of both changes and the player dropped to accommodate Archer will be closely analysed by Indian fans and selectors ahead of what promises to be a keenly contested encounter.

For Indian fans, the prospect of facing Archer in a live T20 setting adds a layer of excitement and challenge to the series. The match is set to draw large viewing numbers across TV and online platforms as India look to consolidate their position in the series.
key_facts: Jofra Archer recalled to England's playing XI for 2nd T20I vs India
England made two changes from the first T20I
Match is part of India's ongoing tour of England

stories.headline: Diljit Dosanjh's Punjab 95 finally streams 'uncut' after three-year censorship battle
stories.what: Diljit Dosanjh's long-delayed film Punjab 95 has arrived on OTT in an uncut version after a three-year fight with censors, released under a new title. The film, which dramatises the story of human rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra and the enforced disappearances of Sikhs in 1990s Punjab, had been stuck in limbo since it was first screened at film festivals. Its OTT debut marks the end of a protracted battle over certification and content.
stories.lens: A film suppressed for three years by censorship concerns now reaches millions of Indian viewers uncut — a rare win for artistic freedom over regulatory gatekeeping.
stories.article:
Diljit Dosanjh's Punjab 95 has finally reached audiences across India, streaming in its uncut form on OTT under a new title after a censorship battle that stretched across three years. The film, which portrays the true story of human rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra who documented the secret cremation of thousands of Sikhs allegedly killed in extrajudicial encounters by Punjab Police in the 1990s, had been repeatedly stalled by the Central Board of Film Certification.

The film was first shown at the Toronto International Film Festival and generated significant buzz for both Dosanjh's performance and director Honey Trehan's unflinching treatment of a dark chapter in Indian history. However, it could not secure a theatrical release in India, with reports indicating that the CBFC demanded cuts that the filmmakers were unwilling to make, leaving the project in an extended limbo.

The decision to release it on OTT — and uncut at that — represents a significant moment for Indian cinema's ongoing negotiation between creative expression and regulatory oversight. Streaming platforms have increasingly become a refuge for films that face hurdles in the theatrical certification process, offering filmmakers a route to audiences that bypasses some of the more contentious demands of the CBFC.

For Dosanjh, who has emerged as one of Hindi cinema's most bankable and critically respected stars in recent years, the release is also a personal vindication. The film arriving in its intended form, even if under a different title, ensures that the story of Khalra — recognised internationally as a human rights hero — can finally be seen by Indian viewers as the filmmakers intended.
key_facts: Punjab 95 stars Diljit Dosanjh as human rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra
Film was blocked from Indian theatrical release after CBFC certification dispute
Now streaming uncut on OTT under a new title after a three-year battle
Directed by Honey Trehan; previously screened at international film festivals

stories.headline: Alpha marks a turning point: Women finally lead Indian spy thrillers after six decades
stories.what: A new analysis argues that the Alia Bhatt-led spy thriller Alpha represents a landmark shift in Indian cinema — the first time in six decades that women have been placed at the centre of the espionage genre, rather than its margins. The piece traces how the genre, long dominated by male protagonists, is being reimagined with female agency at its core. Alpha's arrival signals a broader industry reckoning with who gets to be the hero of India's biggest-budget action films.
stories.lens: For decades, Indian women in spy films were props or love interests; Alpha's positioning of a female lead at the genre's heart reflects a genuine commercial and creative shift that viewers and filmmakers alike have been pushing for.
stories.article:
Indian cinema's spy thriller genre is undergoing its most significant transformation in six decades, with the Alia Bhatt-led Alpha cited as the clearest evidence yet that women are finally taking command of a space long reserved for male heroes.

Since the genre took shape in the 1960s — shaped by the global James Bond wave and its Indian imitators — the template has remained stubbornly consistent: a male operative, physically dominant and romantically irresistible, with women orbiting him as love interests, informants, or adversaries. Films across Hindi, Tamil, and Telugu cinema have reinforced this structure across generations, even as their production values grew more sophisticated.

Alpha, directed by Shiv Rawail and produced under the YRF Spy Universe banner, places Alia Bhatt in the lead role of a RAW agent — not as a supporting character within a male operative's story, but as the protagonist whose mission drives the entire narrative. The film's development and marketing have been explicitly framed around this distinction, and commentary around its release has focused on what it means for the industry's willingness to back women in physically demanding, high-stakes lead roles with the same budgets and promotional muscle typically reserved for male stars.

The shift is not merely symbolic. It reflects changing audience demographics and a growing recognition that female-led films can deliver commercial returns at scale — a case made convincingly by a run of successful women-led productions in recent years. Whether Alpha's box-office performance consolidates or complicates that argument will be closely watched.
key_facts: Alpha stars Alia Bhatt as a lead RAW spy operative
First female-led spy thriller in Indian cinema in six decades, per analysis
Directed by Shiv Rawail under YRF Spy Universe
Marks a shift from decades of male-dominated espionage film formula

stories.headline: Rekha's co-star refused to shoot with her over appearance: 'I was plump, unattractive'
stories.what: A Bollywood co-star of Rekha has revealed that they once refused to do a photo shoot with the actress, citing concerns about her appearance at the time and describing themselves as feeling "plump" and "unattractive" in comparison. The anecdote sheds light on the intense body-image pressures and interpersonal dynamics within the Hindi film industry during Rekha's early career. Rekha herself underwent a dramatic physical transformation in her early years that became a defining moment in Bollywood lore.
stories.lens: The story is a striking window into the brutal appearance-based judgements that shaped — and sometimes derailed — careers in Bollywood's earlier era, pressures that many in the industry are only now speaking about openly.
stories.article:
A candid revelation about Bollywood's past has surfaced, with one of Rekha's former co-stars admitting they once refused to participate in a photo shoot alongside the actress — not out of rivalry, but out of a deeply personal insecurity about their own appearance, describing themselves at the time as "plump" and "unattractive."

The disclosure offers a rare, unguarded glimpse into the body-image anxieties that pervaded the Hindi film industry during Rekha's formative years in cinema. Rekha, who debuted as a teenager and faced significant public commentary about her weight and looks before transforming into one of the industry's most glamorous icons, was herself no stranger to appearance-based criticism during that period.

The unnamed co-star's admission inverts the usual narrative: rather than dismissing Rekha, they were paralysed by their own self-perceived inadequacy beside her. It is a humanising account that speaks to the relentless physical scrutiny all actors — not just women — faced in that era, and the psychological toll it exacted.

Rekha remains one of Hindi cinema's most enduring and enigmatic figures, celebrated for her performances in films like Umrao Jaan and Silsila. Stories from her early career continue to attract significant interest, both for what they reveal about the actress herself and for what they expose about the industry's often harsh internal culture during the 1970s and 1980s.
key_facts: Rekha's co-star admitted refusing a photo shoot citing own appearance insecurities
Co-star described feeling 'plump' and 'unattractive' at the time
Rekha famously underwent a dramatic image transformation in her early career
Rekha is known for iconic films including Umrao Jaan and Silsila

stories.headline: Farah Khan confirms parents Zeenat Aman and Sanjay Khan were married: 'He divorced her later'
stories.what: Farah Khan, daughter of veteran Bollywood actress Zeenat Aman and actor-producer Sanjay Khan, has publicly confirmed that her parents were indeed married — and that Sanjay Khan later divorced Zeenat Aman. The revelation puts to rest decades of speculation about the nature of their relationship, which had never been formally acknowledged before. Zeenat Aman had a tumultuous personal life that was widely reported on in the 1980s, including her relationship with Sanjay Khan.
stories.lens: A decades-old mystery about one of Bollywood's most iconic actresses is finally answered by her own daughter — a rare, candid moment of family truth in an industry known for its carefully guarded personal histories.
stories.article:
One of Bollywood's longest-running personal mysteries has been resolved by an eyewitness with the clearest possible view: Farah Khan, the daughter of Zeenat Aman and Sanjay Khan, has confirmed that her parents were formally married, and that Sanjay Khan subsequently divorced Zeenat Aman.

Zeenat Aman, one of Hindi cinema's most celebrated actresses of the 1970s and 1980s, was known to have had a close and controversial relationship with Sanjay Khan, who was already married at the time. The nature of their union — whether formal or otherwise — had remained a subject of rumour and speculation for decades, with neither party having ever made an unambiguous public statement.

Farah Khan's confirmation changes that. By stating plainly that a marriage took place and that it ended in divorce, she provides the clearest account yet of what transpired between her parents. The disclosure is especially significant given that Zeenat Aman experienced a highly publicised and reportedly violent episode during that period of her life, which made her relationship with Sanjay Khan a touchstone in broader conversations about women's safety and dignity in the film industry.

Zeenat Aman, who has experienced a remarkable cultural renaissance in recent years through her candid and warmly received presence on social media, has spoken openly about many aspects of her past — though the precise legal status of her relationship with Sanjay Khan had remained unaddressed. Her daughter's statement now fills that gap, adding a definitive chapter to one of Indian cinema's most storied personal histories.
key_facts: Farah Khan confirms Zeenat Aman and Sanjay Khan were legally married
Sanjay Khan later divorced Zeenat Aman, per Farah Khan
Relationship had been subject to speculation for decades
Zeenat Aman is one of Bollywood's most iconic actresses of the 1970s–80s

stories.headline: Beyond Dhurandhar and Border: The 10 underrated Hindi films that have defined 2026 so far
stories.what: A curated list from The Indian Express highlights ten underrated Hindi films that have made a significant mark in 2026, beyond the headline blockbusters Dhurandhar and Border. The roundup draws attention to smaller, less commercially visible productions that critics and audiences have found rewarding, offering a broader picture of the health and diversity of Hindi cinema this year. The piece serves as a corrective to the blockbuster-dominated conversation that tends to crowd out mid-range and indie films.
stories.lens: With Bollywood's conversation dominated by a handful of mega-releases, this list is a useful guide for the millions of Hindi film viewers looking for quality cinema that isn't getting the marketing spend of a big-budget franchise film.
stories.article:
Hindi cinema in 2026 has been dominated in public conversation by blockbusters like Dhurandhar and Border, but a new editorial from The Indian Express argues that the year's most interesting work has often happened in the films receiving the least attention.

The publication's list of ten underrated Hindi films that have defined 2026 so far functions as both a critical corrective and a practical guide for audiences who feel the mainstream discourse has narrowed around a handful of franchise entries and star-driven spectacles. By naming specific films beyond the marquee titles, the piece makes the case that the ecosystem of Hindi cinema remains varied and alive with storytelling that doesn't always make it to the top of the box-office charts or the front pages of entertainment coverage.

The exercise is particularly timely in a year when the industry has been grappling with questions of formula versus originality, and whether the commercial pressure towards sequels and known intellectual properties is crowding out fresh voices. The films highlighted in the list represent a cross-section of genres, budgets, and sensibilities that together paint a more complete picture of where Hindi cinema actually is in 2026.

For regular cinema-goers, the list offers a useful entry point into films that may have had limited theatrical runs or modest OTT promotion, but which critics argue deserve a broader audience. In an era of content abundance, curation of this kind plays an increasingly important role in connecting viewers with work that might otherwise slip past them.
key_facts: List covers 10 underrated Hindi films of 2026 beyond Dhurandhar and Border
Curated by The Indian Express as a critical corrective to blockbuster-dominated coverage
Highlights smaller productions that received limited mainstream attention
Reflects broader debate about formula vs. originality in Bollywood
